title: Money Out
description: What leaves the Stripe account: refunds, disputes and their penalty fees, and non-cash concessions. Sourced from Stripe's own balance-transaction ledger, so it includes outflows made outside this bot (the Stripe Dashboard included). ORDINARY PROCESSING FEES ARE EXCLUDED FROM EVERY TOTAL — they are the cost of taking money, not money lost, and live in their own row at the bottom. Amounts are net of reversals, in major units. For staff-activity counts use the 'Billing: Support Events' dashboard instead: its events describe what the team did, and several of them describe the same money.

panels.title: Total lost

targets.query:
from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "money_out")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "amount_minor")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.category != "stripe_fee")
  |> sum()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ r with _value: r._value / 100.0 }))

panels.description: Everything we LOST in the window, net of reversals: refunds, disputes, chargeback fees and concessions. Ordinary Stripe processing fees are deliberately excluded — that is the cost of taking money, not money lost, and folding it in would make this number climb with healthy revenue.

panels.title: Losses per day by category

targets.query:
from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "money_out")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "amount_minor")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.category != "stripe_fee")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.category != "refund_failure" and r.category != "dispute_reversal")
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value", "category"])
  |> group(columns: ["category"])
  |> aggregateWindow(every: 1d, fn: sum, createEmpty: true)
  |> fill(value: 0.0)
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ r with _value: r._value / 100.0 }))

panels.description: Stacked daily losses. Reversals (refunds that failed, disputes we won) are EXCLUDED here so the bars stay readable — money coming back would stack downward and smear every bar. See 'Reversals per day' for those, and the tiles above for the net figures, which do subtract them.

panels.description: webhook = seen live (this is what catches Stripe Dashboard refunds); sweep = found by the reconcile tick; backfill = historical import; action = booked by one of our own panels.

panels.title: Ledger reconcile lag

targets.query:
from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "money_out_sweep" and r._field == "lag_seconds")
  |> aggregateWindow(every: 10m, fn: max, createEmpty: false)

panels.description: How far behind Stripe the mirror is. A climbing line means outflows are happening that the ledger has not seen: check the reconcile looper and the Stripe key.

panels.title: Reconcile errors

targets.query:

  |> aggregateWindow(every: 1h, fn: sum, createEmpty: true)
  |> fill(value: 0.0)

panels.description: Anything above zero for a sustained period means the ledger is drifting from Stripe.

panels.title: Context: not losses, never counted
panels.description: Processing fees and never-collected invoices. Neither is money lost — a fee is what taking money costs, and a voided invoice is revenue that never arrived. Both dwarf real losses by volume, so neither is included in any total above.
